query: we've got this processTransaction() in our billing service thats up to 9 params now, half of them booleans like isRetry, skipValidation. every time someone adds a feature they bolt another flag on it. i want a writeup i can bring to the team explaining exactly why this is a problem and what we actually do about it

my teammate keeps saying my code has too many tiny functions and that his 200-line method is 'easier to follow because its all in one place'. we've gone in circles on this in PR review twice now. is there an actual principle here or is it just taste

we check the user's remaining credits at the start of checkout and then again right before we charge them. someone on the team says the second check is redundant duplication and wants it removed. i have a bad feeling about it but i cant articulate why

we're about 3 weeks from launching our first real customer-facing service. before we go i want someone to go through the design and tell me what operational stuff we've completely failed to think about - the kind of thing that bites you at 3am

our service has application-prod.yml, application-staging.yml and application-dev.yml all committed to the repo with different db hosts and a couple of api keys sitting in them. i know this is bad but i need to explain to my lead *how* bad and what the actual fix looks like

putting the design doc for our new notification service in docs/notifications-design.md. before we start building can you go through it and flag anything that violates basic engineering principles - id rather hear it now than in code review

need to decide whether to keep our nightly batch processing on the on-prem vms or move it to lambda. cost is the main driver but i dont want to get locked into aws either

this UserService class is 800 lines. i want you to actually break it up into smaller classes - behavior needs to stay identical, we have decent test coverage so you can verify as you go
can you review the diff on my current branch before i open the PR, mostly looking for bugs i might have missed
we're getting audited next month. go through our auth code and find anything thats an actual vulnerability - sql injection, missing authz checks, that kind of thing
we have basically no idea whats happening in prod right now. i need actual logging and metrics instrumented in this service - prometheus, structured logs, the works
